summary.text: Amanda Cappelletti is a Democratic member of the Pennsylvania Senate who represents the 17th Senatorial District, covering parts of Montgomery and Delaware Counties.
An attorney with a master's in public health, she is the Democratic chair of the Senate Judiciary Committee.

paragraphs.text: Cappelletti grew up in Boyertown, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Boyertown Area Senior High, according to her official biography.
She attended Chestnut Hill College for her undergraduate degree and received her law degree and Master in Public Health from Temple University.
She got her start in government on the East Norriton Board of Supervisors.

She worked in Harrisburg with former Representative Donna Bullock and as a fellow for the ACLU of Pennsylvania, and was in the first group awarded the William Penn Fellowship through the Governor's office, working at the Office of Child Development and Early Learning and then the Department of Human Services.
She is also the former director of policy at Planned Parenthood.
In the Senate, she has prioritized safe and healthy communities, including action on climate change and gun violence, and she co-chairs the Pennsylvania Women's Health Caucus.
She lives in East Norriton with her husband, Gregory McQuiston, and their daughters.
